b082.name: the uridine evidence paragraph, fifth try (after the tell panel)
b082.text: The tool: Uridine monophosphate (UMP). There's no study showing that "UMP cures DAWS", only more basic research on what uridine, choline, and DHA do in the brain. All three get carried in the blood to the brain, which uses them to make the fatty membranes at its synapses (circulating precursors for brain phosphatide / synaptic membrane synthesis). Wurtman's research group found that giving the three together can increase synaptic membrane components and synaptic proteins, and that in animals, adding UMP to DHA made the neurons grow more new connection points (DHA-induced dendritic spine formation). And old rats that got UMP in their food released more dopamine when their neurons were stimulated with potassium, and grew more nerve fibers. So it's plausible that it works on the synapses this way, but using it for DAWS in people means carefully extrapolating from those studies and from anecdotes like Scott's.
b082.why: the panel's agreed tells on try 3 fixed: "so the best evidence we have is more basic than that" said as "only more basic research on what ... do in the brain"; the plain meaning first and one term after it in brackets, with no "that is," restatement; "cautious extrapolation" said as "carefully extrapolating"; "potassium" back. The panel read it again and still agrees on both brackets and the closing hedge

b083.name: Scott's signal, fifth try (after the tell panel)
b083.text: Scott was already getting choline from eggs and DHA/EPA from fish oil, and after he added a standard dose of UMP he had a striking response within a day. His vivid dreams came back, with childhood memories in them, his psychedelic tolerance seemed to drop, and his ketamine/LSD cravings fell off hard. In the right person, a response like that can be a clean signal that the brain was starved for what it needs to rebuild the membranes and dopamine receptors at its synapses, even if there's no way to tell whether UMP rebuilt his D3 receptors overnight.

The panel read it again and still agrees on all three sentences
